title: Index Card Story Show-Not-Tell Card Pack
audience: Families, homeschool groups, tutors, and adult-led writing tables for writers ages 7-11.
sessionLength: 16 printable show-not-tell cards plus adult guide tools, show-not-tell routines, take-home show slips, and optional share prompts
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.

cover.headline: Index Card Story Show-Not-Tell Card Pack
cover.subhead: Sixteen paper cards help writers turn plain fictional lines into visible clues, object actions, place signals, gestures, texture details, and revised sentences.

adultGuide.title: Index Card Show-Not-Tell Adult Guide
bullets: Print the index cards, blank clue rows, and revision slips before the adult-led paper session.
Begin with one plain line and coach the writer to show it through visible clue, object action, place signal, character gesture, and paper-safe sound or texture detail.
Keep every example fictional, broad, offline, and guided by an adult.
Use one card per sentence so the page stays small enough for ages 7-11.
Replace any actual person detail or narrow outside fact with a made-up name, broad story place, or pretend object.
End each card with a revised sentence that shows the idea without naming it too directly.

showRoutines.name: Plain Line Clue Row
showRoutines.bestFor: Writers who tell the idea first and need a simple path toward showing it.
steps: The adult reads one plain line from an index card.
The writer names the idea the line currently tells.
The adult points to five clue slots: visible clue, object action, place signal, character gesture, and sound/texture detail.
The writer writes one revised sentence using two clue slots: ____________________.

showRoutines.name: Object Action Swap
showRoutines.bestFor: Turning a flat sentence into a sentence with a visible story object.
steps: The adult circles the object in a plain line.
The writer chooses one gentle action the object can do, such as lean, tap, wobble, or slide.
The adult asks what the object action helps the reader notice.
The writer writes one object action sentence: ____________________.

showRoutines.name: Place Signal Pass
showRoutines.bestFor: Showing a broad fictional place without naming it too plainly.
steps: The adult covers the direct place word in a plain line.
The writer chooses a place signal such as an arch, shelf, banner, puddle, or lantern.
The adult asks what the signal tells the reader about the pretend place.
The writer writes one place signal sentence: ____________________.

showRoutines.name: Gesture Before Feeling
showRoutines.bestFor: Replacing a named feeling with a character gesture the reader can see.
steps: The adult reads a plain line that tells how a fictional character feels.
The writer chooses one character gesture, such as toe tapping, sleeve smoothing, or eyebrow lifting.
The adult asks which feeling the gesture lets the reader infer.
The writer writes one gesture-first sentence: ____________________.

showRoutines.name: Sound Texture Thread
showRoutines.bestFor: Adding one paper-safe sound or texture detail to make the moment easier to imagine.
steps: The adult rereads the plain line and asks where a tiny sensory clue could fit.
The writer chooses one sound word or texture phrase a reader can imagine from print.
The adult asks whether the clue supports the visible action instead of distracting from it.
The writer writes one sound or texture detail sentence: ____________________.

showRoutines.name: Revised Sentence Stack
showRoutines.bestFor: Combining the strongest clues into one clear revised sentence.
steps: The adult places the plain line at the top of the index card stack.
The writer chooses the strongest visible clue and one supporting clue.
The adult asks which telling word can be removed.
The writer writes the final revised sentence: ____________________.

cards.title: Compass Craft Academy Steady Needle
cards.showSkill: show careful choice through object action
cards.useCase: Adult-led printable index card show-not-tell card for changing a plain compass sentence into careful object action and place signals: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place two invented compass-craft options beside the card and ask for clues that show careful choosing: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Show the crafter being careful by naming what the paper compass does and how the character checks it: ____________________.
cards.plainLinePrompt: Plain line: The compass crafter was careful. Copy or change the plain sentence before showing the care: ____________________.
cards.visibleCluePrompt: Visible clue: Show careful work with one aligned arrow, centered bead, tiny fold mark, or neat pencil tick: ____________________.
cards.objectActionPrompt: Object action: Make the paper needle, bead marker, folded arrow, or compass card swivel, settle, pause, or line up: ____________________.
cards.placeSignalPrompt: Place signal: Add one craft bench, supply tray, marker rail, or folded-paper stand that shows where the careful choice happens: ____________________.
cards.characterGesturePrompt: Character gesture: Show the crafter's care with one slow breath, narrowed eyes, steady hand, or second check: ____________________.
cards.soundOrTexturePrompt: Paper-safe sound or texture: Add a soft paper creak, bead tap, smooth fold, pencil tick, or crisp card corner: ____________________.
cards.sentenceFramePrompt: Sentence frame: Instead of naming care, write: The compass crafter ____________________.
cards.reviseShowPrompt: Revise show: Replace the plain adjective with one compass action and one small checking gesture: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Mark the careful object action first, then write the revised sentence below it: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-on line: Invent another compass-craft sentence where careful choice appears through a tool clue: ____________________.

cards.title: Binding Day Boardwalk Clasp Promise
cards.showSkill: show pride through a promise and page detail
cards.useCase: Adult-led printable index card show-not-tell card for turning a plain boardwalk sentence into page clues, gesture, and texture detail: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place a pretend folded-page card beside this prompt and keep the promise small, kind, and fully invented: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Show the page helper's pride through a careful object detail and a gentle action, without naming the feeling: ____________________.
cards.plainLinePrompt: Plain line: The page helper felt proud. Copy or change the plain sentence before showing pride through details: ____________________.
cards.visibleCluePrompt: Visible clue: Show pride with one straightened clasp, neat thread loop, polished page edge, or tucked promise slip: ____________________.
cards.objectActionPrompt: Object action: Make the booklet clasp, folded page, thread loop, or sign card close, shine, settle, or line up: ____________________.
cards.placeSignalPrompt: Place signal: Add one boardwalk rail, booklet stand, paper booth, or page table clue that shows the promise has been kept: ____________________.
cards.characterGesturePrompt: Character gesture: Show the helper's pride with one small nod, careful smile, lifted chin, or gentle pat on the page: ____________________.
cards.soundOrTexturePrompt: Paper-safe sound or texture: Add a clasp click, thread brush, smooth page edge, crisp fold, or soft card tap: ____________________.
cards.sentenceFramePrompt: Sentence frame: Instead of naming pride, write: The page helper ____________________.
cards.reviseShowPrompt: Revise show: Replace the feeling word with one kept-promise clue and one page-helper gesture: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Choose one clasp or page clue, then write a sentence that shows pride silently: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Carry-on line: Make one more boardwalk index card where a page detail shows a gentle promise kept: ____________________.
